description: Ninja Creami deals UK: today's best prices on the original, Deluxe, XL and Scoop & Swirl, which to buy, and the Black Friday price to wait for.
intro:

body:
## Which Ninja Creami should you buy?

There are four Creami models on sale in the UK. They all work the same way: you freeze a base in a tub overnight, then the machine shaves and churns it into ice cream in a few minutes. The differences are tub size, number of programmes and whether it does soft serve.

- **Creami NC300UK (original):** seven programmes, including ice cream, gelato, sorbet, light ice cream, milkshake and smoothie bowl. Tubs hold about 490ml. List price £199.99. **Best for most people**, especially couples and small families.
- **Creami Deluxe NC501UK:** ten programmes, adding frozen drinks, frappés and Italian ice, and larger 709ml tubs. List price £249.99. Worth it if you make big batches or want slushy drinks.
- **Creami XL NC601UK:** the 2026 model, with eleven programmes (including frozen yoghurt, dairy-free and a protein setting) and two 710ml tubs. Its dual mode makes two flavours from one base. Prices so far range from £249.99 to £259.99.
- **Creami Scoop & Swirl NC701UK:** 13 programmes, six for soft serve and six for scoop ice cream, with a lever that pipes soft serve straight into a cone. It uses smaller 480ml tubs. List price £349.99. **The one to buy if you want soft serve.**

If you mainly want healthy, high-protein or low-sugar ice cream, the original does that just as well as the pricier models. Pay more only for bigger tubs, frozen drinks or soft serve.

## Good prices to look for

These are the prices worth paying, based on last Black Friday and recent price history:

- **NC300UK:** £119.99 was the lowest-ever price at Amazon on Black Friday 2025. Anything under £150 is good; today's best is £169.90.
- **NC501UK:** we found no reliable Black Friday low from last year. Around £200 is a good price, which is where AO is today.
- **NC601UK:** price trackers show a three-month low of £209. Aim for £210 or less.
- **NC701UK Scoop & Swirl:** £273.99 at Amazon on Black Friday 2025. Under £280 is good; today's best is £289.

## When do Ninja Creami prices drop?

The biggest cuts usually land in Black Friday week, which starts on 19 November at Amazon this year and runs to Cyber Monday on 30 November. Argos, John Lewis and Very tend to match each other within a day or two. Last year Ninja's own Black Friday offers included free accessories as well as price cuts. Amazon's Prime Day in the summer is the other good time to buy. Our [Ninja Black Friday deals guide](/guides/ninja-black-friday-deals-2026/) has target prices for Ninja's air fryers, Slushi and blenders too, and our [Black Friday 2026 hub](/black-friday/) covers every brand.

## Tips before you buy

- **Buy spare tubs.** Each tub needs about 24 hours in the freezer, so with only the tubs in the box you can make one or two batches a day. Spare tubs are model-specific: Deluxe and XL tubs don't fit the original, and the Swirl uses its own tubs.
- **Check freezer space.** The Deluxe and XL tubs are tall, so measure your freezer drawers first.
- **It's noisy.** Processing takes a couple of minutes and sounds like a blender.
- **Lakeland no longer sells the NC300UK or NC501UK**, so compare Argos, John Lewis, Very, AO and Amazon instead.

### Which Ninja Creami is best?

For most people, the original NC300UK. It makes the same ice cream as the dearer models and costs the least. Choose the Scoop & Swirl if you want soft serve, or the Deluxe or XL for bigger batches.

### Is the Ninja Creami worth it?

If you'd use it at least weekly, yes. It's especially good for protein or low-sugar ice cream, which is expensive to buy ready made. The catch is the overnight freezing, so it isn't for spur-of-the-moment treats.

### Will the Ninja Creami be cheaper on Black Friday?

Very likely. Last year the original dropped to £119.99 and the Scoop & Swirl to £273.99, both below today's best prices.

### Can you use Creami Deluxe tubs in the original Creami?

No. The Deluxe and XL use larger tubs that don't fit the NC300UK, and the Swirl has its own tubs. Always buy spares made for your model.
